title: Density of the product Gaussian law
statement: Let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb R$. For every measurable set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, the product measure $\gamma\otimes\gamma$ assigns $A$ the nonnegative extended real integral of the planar standard Gaussian density: $(\gamma\otimes\gamma)(A)=\int_A d_2(x,y)\,d(x,y)$, where $d_2(x,y)=(2\pi)^{-1}\exp(-(x^2+y^2)/2)$.
replaced: Let $\gamma$ be the standard real Gaussian probability measure. For every measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, $(\gamma\otimes\gamma)(A)=\int_A(2\pi)^{-1}e^{-(x^2+y^2)/2}\,dx\,dy$, where the integral is nonnegative and extended-valued.
